children: By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M
Indian shares slipped marginally on Friday, as IT stocks dropped after a four-session rally to offset broader gains from returning foreign inflows.
The Nifty 50
slipped 0.16% to 25,845.1 while the Sensex
eased 0.29% to 84,077.8, as of 10:03 a.m. IST.
Eleven of the 16 major sectors logged gains. The broader small-caps
and mid-caps
gained about 1% each.

The 50-stock Nifty index and the Sensex are up 0.2% each so far this week, consolidating after a nearly 15% surge over the last four weeks that saw Indian benchmarks outperforming Asian and emerging market peers.
The rally in November was driven by record monthly foreign inflows, worth $15.5 billion, aided by a global AI trade reversal and robust earnings.
Brent crude futures

hovered around $96.5 per barrel, rising 4.2% over the week as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from the conflict-hit region.

"The rise in Brent crude is negative news in the context of rising inflation in India, while the US tariff proposal is another threat," said VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments.
After the recent rally, "a consolidation phase appears likely in the near term," Vijayakumar said.
IT index
fell 1.5% after rising 8% in the last four sessions.
Among stocks, Waaree Renewable Technologies
surged 10% after receiving a letter of award for a 120 MWp turnkey EPC project.
Freight wagon manufacturer Texmaco Rail
gained 2.6% on winning an order worth $6.02 million from Utkal Alumina International for supply of 108 railway wagons.
Engineering, procurement and construction firm EMS
added 2% on securing a $2.8 million order from the National Highways Authority of India.
Coal India
unit Mahanadi Coalfields (MHAN.NS) fell 1.5% in its trading debutk.
Jet Freight Logistics
fell 2% after the logistics firm said India's markets regulator summoned its chairman and managing director as part of an ongoing investigation into the company.
